method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text, seat-neutral core with regulative rules where the text states duties, and a seat layer for the resident individual taxpayer, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE (nonresidents, tax years other than 2026-2027, New York AGI over $100,000 and s 603 lump sums answer `not covered`, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: New York Tax Law Article 22, NYSenate.gov Open Legislation, retrieved 2026-10-24, each section at its most recent revision (s 601: 2025-07-11; s 606: 2026-10-23; s 612: 2026-09-04; others per the .meta.json), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/ny-tax-law-art22-selected.txt. Tax years 2026 and 2027.

scope: Resident individuals, tax years 2026 and 2027: s 605(b)(1); s 651(a)(1); ss 651(a), 652(a), (b); s 612(a) with (c)(3), (3-a), (3-c) computed and other modifications as inputs; s 611(a); s 613; s 614 (the s 614(f) adjustment an input); s 616(a); s 601(a), (b), (c) para (1)(B)(vii), (viii); s 606(b); s 606(c-1)(1-a)(B)-(E), (2); s 606(d)(1), (2). Out: nonresidents and part-year residents, estates and trusts, s 601(d)/(d-1) recapture (NY AGI over $100,000), s 603, s 615, other s 606 credits, NYC and Yonkers taxes.
